2020_151_061620mtg.paragraph: Troy School District's Board of Education agenda packet for the regular meeting of June 16, 2020, held at 7:00 PM by Zoom, combines a public hearing on the 2020/2021 proposed budget with the 2019/2020 final budget amendment, the April 2020 Treasurer's Report and check register, retiree recognition, and business items covering asbestos abatement, video surveillance, SMART display appliances, iPads, and the amended International Academy Consortium Agreement. The budget presentation models three foundation allowance reduction scenarios of $200, $400 and $700 per pupil against a 2020-21 general fund appropriation of $161,272,639, with enrollment projected flat at 13,098.

**Meeting and agenda**
Troy School District Board of Education, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (248.823.4000), regular meeting of June 16, 2020, 7:00 PM by Zoom videoconference (https://zoom.us/j/2489521600, Meeting ID 248 952 1600); cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW). Agenda: public hearing on the 2020/2021 proposed budget; recognition of retirees; consent agenda (May 5 workshop and May 19 meeting minutes, Treasurer's Report – April 2020, 2019/2020 Budget Amendment, 2020/2021 Budget Appropriations Resolution, Food Service Contract Renewal, Equity and Excellence Policy adoption); Extended Learning report; considerations on Niles asbestos abatement, security cameras, smart display appliances and iPads; and the International Academy Amended Consortium Agreement. Board members: Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff (Secretary Gary N. Hauff), Philippart, Schmidt (President), Wilson; Superintendent Dr. Machesky; Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services.

**2020-21 budget presentation**
Taxable value rose from a 2019 total of $4,089,904,210 (homestead $2,761,994,935; non-homestead $1,327,909,275) to a 2020 total of $4,236,286,120 (homestead $2,853,891,030; non-homestead $1,382,395,090), labeled a 3.58% increase. Proposed 2020/21 millage components: S.E.T. 6.0000, hold harmless 4.6750, debt 4.1000, sinking fund 0.9826; homestead total 15.7576, non-homestead total 29.0826. Assumptions: enrollment unchanged at 13,098; a 1.65% increase in the PA 152 health insurance hard cap; retirement effective rate rising from 27.50% to 28.21%; FICA at 7.65%; a reduction of 15 TEA positions through attrition; purchased services up about $1.2 million or 5%; supplies down about $1.2 million or 17%.

| 2020-21 scenario | Foundation allowance | Revenue | Fund balance | Fund balance % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Projected 2019-20 | $9,315 | $160,466,086 | $26,765,254 | 16.82% |
| Scenario 1 (-$200) | $9,115 | $157,433,393 | $22,926,008 | 14.22% |
| Scenario 2 (-$400) | $8,915 | $154,883,013 | $20,375,628 | 12.63% |
| Scenario 3 (-$700) | $8,615 | $151,057,442 | $16,550,057 | 10.26% |

Expense is held at $161,272,639 in all three scenarios. A "three-tiered strategy" of reductions, fund balance and shared sacrifice is outlined for FY 2020-21, 2021-22 and 2022-23.

**April 2020 Treasurer's Report**
Total check disbursements $22,639,669.34 (general fund $5,191,018.67; special revenue funds $158,682.29; other funds $17,289,968.38), ACH debits $35,746.86, outgoing wire transfers $2,068,254.01, P-Card purchases $30,435.12, prior period voids ($6,809.79), total disbursements in period $24,767,295.54. Debt funds accounted for $15,134,680.50 and capital projects funds $2,114,850.70.

**Budget actions**
The 2019-20 amendment appropriates $159,107,325 in the general fund, with ending fund balance June 30 of $26,765,254 and excess revenues of $1,358,761. The 2020-21 appropriations resolution levies 18.0000 mills non-homestead, 10.6750 mills on commercial personal property, 4.6750 mills homestead, 4.1000 mills debt retirement and 0.9826 mills sinking fund, and appropriates $161,272,639 (general fund), $3,413,481 (food service), $2,228,200 (Troy Career Center), $2,624,140 (community service), $2,144,375 (preschool), $166,773 (facilities rental), $2,250,000 (student activities), $0 (capital maintenance), $4,028,933 (2016 capital projects), $7,500,000 (2019 capital projects), $1,031,713 (2020 capital projects), $3,955,000 (sinking fund) and $17,375,562 (debt service).

**Business items**
Niles asbestos abatement to Quality Environmental, $117,220.00 plus 10% contingency $11,722.00, total request $128,942.00; video surveillance to ROK Systems, $198,352.69; 150 SMART AM40 appliances from Tierney, $36,375; iPads and cases from Apple Computers, $2,029,965 from the 2019 Capital Projects Funds. Food service contract renewed with Chartwells for 2020/2021.

Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff (Secretary Gary N. Hauff), Philippart, Schmidt (President) and Wilson; Superintendent Dr. Machesky; Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services.

**Budget presentation.** Twelve funds are described: General Fund (1xx), Debt Retirement Funds (3xx), Capital Projects Funds (416, 418, 419, 420), Sinking Fund (498), Capital Maintenance Fund (499), Food Service Fund (520), TCC Grant Fund (529), Community Service Fund (530), Troy Preschool Fund (531), Facility Rental Fund (535) and Student Activities Fund (570). Taxable value: 2019 homestead $2,761,994,935 and non-homestead $1,327,909,275, total $4,089,904,210; 2020 homestead $2,853,891,030 and non-homestead $1,382,395,090, total $4,236,286,120, a 3.58% increase. Proposed 2020/21 millage components are S.E.T. 6.0000, hold harmless 4.6750, debt 4.1000, sinking fund 0.9826 and the statewide 18.0000 non-homestead mills, giving totals of 15.7576 homestead and 29.0826 non-homestead, against 15.9693 and 29.0857 in 2019/20.

Assumptions for 2020-21: enrollment 13,098, no change from the current year; foundation allowance scenarios of $200, $400 and $700 per-pupil reduction; a reduction of 15 (TEA) through attrition; a 1.65% increase in the PA 152 health insurance hard cap rate; the retirement effective rate rising from 27.50% to 28.21%; FICA unchanged at 7.65%; purchased services up approximately $1.2 million or 5%; supplies down approximately $1.2 million or 17% after the 2019-20 science curriculum adoption. Foundation allowance was $9,275 in 2008-09 through 2010-11 and $9,315 in 2019-20, becoming $9,115, $8,915 and $8,615 under the three scenarios; a $248.18 20J reduction occurred in 2009-10. Enrollment history: 12,563, 12,717, 12,878, 13,081, 13,096, 13,098 and 13,098 projected.

Revenue, expense and fund balance: 2017-18 $151,774,253 / $150,737,172 / $25,242,472; 2018-19 $153,840,855 / $153,676,834 / $25,406,493; projected 2019-20 $160,466,086 / $159,107,325 / $26,765,254. The 2020-21 scenarios show revenue of $157,433,393, $154,883,013 and $151,057,442 against expense held at $161,272,639, fund balances of $22,926,008, $20,375,628 and $16,550,057, fund balance percentages of 14.22%, 12.63% and 10.26% (16.82% projected for 2019-20), and net revenue of -$3,839,246, -$6,389,626 and -$10,215,197 against $1,358,761 projected. A three-tiered strategy of reductions, fund balance and shared sacrifice is laid out for FY 2020-2021, 2021-2022 and 2022-2023.

**Retirees and prior minutes.** Retirees recognized, names read by Jordan Harris: Nancy Cole, Wendy Gustin, Diane Jakowenko, Deborah Nash, Jo O'Brien and Sue Younan, with district service dates from 1988 to 2000. Consent minutes cover the May 5, 2020 workshop (6:04 p.m. to 8:55 p.m.) and the May 19, 2020 meeting (7:06 p.m., 100 audience members via Zoom), whose actions each carried 7 yes and 0 no: Resolution 20-046 supporting National Teacher Appreciation Week May 4-8, 2020; 20-047 approving the consent agenda including the Oakland Intermediate School District budget; 20-048 approving secondary health materials "Comprehensive Health Skills" and "Essential Health Skills" for $123,041; 20-049 awarding Niles aluminum storefront/glazing to Advanced Building Group for $111,882.00 from the 2020 Capital Projects Fund; 20-050 designating Mr. Steve Gottlieb to the 2020 electoral body for the Oakland Schools Intermediate School District Board of Education and supporting Mr. George Ehlert for a six-year term ending June 30, 2026 at the June 1, 2020 election under Public Act 419 of 2004; and 20-051 voting for Dr. Robert Shaner (Rochester Community Schools) and Mark Dziatczak (Birmingham Public Schools) as International Academy at-large members. Barb Pangle of Hill Elementary was named overall Outstanding Support Staff.

**2019-20 budget amendment (6.D).** Amended appropriations: general fund $159,107,325; food service $3,217,879; Troy Career Center $2,228,200; community service $2,509,783; preschool $1,605,618; facilities rental $161,788; student activities $2,100,000; 2016 capital projects $7,500,000; 2019 capital projects $2,500,000; 2020 capital projects $5,213,775 (adoption); Early Childhood Learning Center capital projects $4,900,286; sinking fund capital projects $3,690,420; debt service $17,856,697. General fund revenues amend to $160,466,086, beginning fund balance $25,406,493, ending fund balance June 30 $26,765,254, excess revenues $1,358,761.

**2020-21 appropriations resolution (6.E).** Millage: non-homestead general operating 18.0000; commercial personal property 10.6750; homestead and industrial personal property 4.6750; debt retirement 4.1000 on all classes; sinking fund 0.9826 on all classes. Appropriations: general fund $161,272,639; food service $3,413,481; Troy Career Center $2,228,200; community service $2,624,140; preschool $2,144,375; facilities rental $166,773; student activities $2,250,000; capital maintenance $0; 2016 capital projects $4,028,933; 2019 capital projects $7,500,000; 2020 capital projects $1,031,713; sinking fund $3,955,000; debt service $17,375,562. General fund revenues: local $41,672,704, state $95,127,294, federal $3,894,025, incoming transfers and other $10,363,419, total $151,057,442; estimated fund balance July 1 $26,765,254; total available to appropriate $177,822,696; total instruction $109,258,988; total support services $51,769,597. The Superintendent is charged with general supervision of budget execution.

**Food service renewal (6.F).** Renewal of the Chartwells contract first approved May 21, 2019, subject to annual Michigan Department of Education and board approval. Rick West's May 26, 2020 letter to Tammy Saul at MDE sets the meal equivalent factor at $3.6475 (from $3.5450, 2.8%), the administrative fee at $12,360 per month for 10 months (from $12,000, 3.0%) and the management fee at $0.0515 (from $0.0500, 3.0%). The FSMC cost-reimbursable renewal runs July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021, district number 50944, renewal year 1 of up to four additional one-year periods, signed 4/15/2020 by Belinda Oakley, CEO Chartwells K12, for Compass Group USA, Inc.

**Equity and Excellence Policy (6.G).** Draft policy committing to differentiated teaching strategies, systematic assessment of institutional climate and implicit bias, and teaching and research about racism, stating outcomes are not presumed by income, race, disability, gender, first language or family background.

**Extended Learning update (8.A).** Presented by Christine DiPilato and Kris Griffor: three fall 2020 scenarios (a regular daily schedule, preferred; blended; fully virtual), with planning aimed first at the virtual case. Surveys drew 3,032 parent responses representing 2,258 secondary students — meaningful work rated always or most of the time by 77% in grades 6-8 and 74% in grades 9-12 — and 2,517 student responses including 1,509 in grades 6-12. A 46-member secondary task force evaluated eight scheduling options, producing a draft with three live 45-minute classes daily and a 30-minute Monday session.

**Business considerations.** Niles Center asbestos abatement (RFP 9907), recommended by NOVA Environmental (Lisa Whitton) and Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance & Operations: Quality Environmental $117,220.00 plus 10% contingency $11,722.00, total project request $128,942.00. Video surveillance RFP #9900, issued March 16, 2020 with seventeen bids opened May 5, 2020 by Convergent Technology Partners (Eric Helsel) for Technology Director Beth Soggs: ROK Systems base bid $173,131.58, recommended award $180,581.57 including Alternate 2 at Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools $3,426.82 and Alternate 3 storage $1,458.17, plus Alternate 1 for the former ITT building $8,325.75 and a 5% contingency of $9,445.37, a project total of $198,352.69 from the 2016 and 2019 Capital Projects Funds. SMART displays: 150 AM40 appliances replacing AM30s bought in May 2017, quoted by Tierney at $36,375.00, VSC at $37,750.00 and AVI-SPL at $71,850.00, award recommended to Tierney. iPads from Apple Computers for $2,029,965 from the 2019 Capital Projects Funds: 5,000 student iPads at $294 plus $56 cases, $1,750,000, and 700 teacher iPads with cases and $49.95 Logitech Crayons, $279,965, on the REMC contract, from series 3 of the technology bond.

**International Academy Amended Consortium Agreement (11.A).** Approves the amendment advanced by the Joint Steering Committee resolution of October 2, 2019 and revised after its April 28, 2020 meeting, with a May 31, 2020 memo and FAQ. Governance moves from 13 members to a five-member Governing Body of the three Fiscal Agents' superintendents plus two at-large members on two-year terms. Fiscal Agents are Bloomfield Hills School District (Okma / IA Bloomfield Hills Campus), Troy School District (Troy Campus / IA East) and Huron Valley Schools (West Campus / IA West). Terms include a two-thirds vote to expel, thirty days to cure default, withdrawal notice by January 15, appeals decided by April 30, campus budgets prepared by March 31 and approved by June 30, tuition rates provided by December 10, a per pupil charge capped at the participating districts' average foundation allowance plus up to 10%, 50% responsibility for unfilled grade-nine shares, five students per share for 2019/2020 with a floor of four, and arbitration in Oakland County under MCL 600.5001 and MCR 3.602. Authorities cited include Act 35 of 1951 (MCL 124.1 et seq.), the Intergovernmental Transfers of Functions and Responsibilities Act (MCL 125.531 et seq.), Revised School Code sections 11a and 1282 (1976 PA 451), the State School Aid Act (1979 PA 94, MCL 388.1601), the Open Meetings Act (Act 267, PA 1976) and the Uniform Budgeting and Accounting Act (PA No. 2 of 1968). Signatories include Berkley, Birmingham, Bloomfield Hills, Clawson, Huron Valley, Lake Orion, Rochester Community, Royal Oak, South Lyon, Avondale, Troy, Waterford and West Bloomfield.
